title: Pagewise KV garbage-collection and kernel-affinity tuning to reduce prefill tail latency
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: We observe p99 prefill/decode latency spikes caused by interleaved allocations and evictions inside the paged KV cache when long-sequence workloads intermix with many short requests. This causes kernel mismatches and head-of-line stalls: large-page allocations trigger heavy compaction that delays small decodes, and the runtime sometimes selects suboptimal kernels because the hot page distribution changes mid-batch.

Goal: Design and implement a pagewise garbage-collection (GC) and kernel-affinity map plus a prefill scheduling throttle that together reduce p95/p99 prefill latency without materially increasing per-token cost. Target: 30-45% reduction in p99 prefill latency on mixed short/long workloads with <= 3% token-cost regression and no regression in p50 latency.

Scope: engineering work on paged KV allocator, eviction policy, per-page residency scores, a compact/merge lane mechanism, kernel-affinity map (page -> preferred kernel variant), and a prefill/decode scheduler that respects affinity and backpressure. This ticket covers design, prototype, perf runs, validation in dedicated infra, and an initial rollout gate for runtime-1.30.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype reduces p99 prefill latency by >=30% on mixed workload replay (internal perf harness)
End-to-end integration test for paged GC with no memory leaks and deterministic compaction under load
Kernel-affinity map persists across restarts and is surfaced in trace spans for debugging
Prefill scheduler honors backpressure thresholds and prevents decode backlog growth beyond configured SLO
Changes gated behind a runtime flag and validated in dedicated small canary before wide rollout
design_notes: Pagewise residency score: combine last-access timestamp, decode frequency, and average token-length to compute a rank used by GC; avoid single-dimension LRU to prevent large-page eviction storms

Compaction lanes: separate light and heavy lanes. Light lane does in-place slot reclamation (cheap) and runs frequently; heavy lane performs cross-page consolidation and runs only when reservoir pressure exceeds threshold or during maintenance windows

Kernel-affinity map: record observed sequence-length distributions per-page at allocation time and bind a preferred kernel variant id. Kernel selection then checks affinity first, falling back to global selector if affinity is stale

Prefill/decode scheduler: implement bucketed scheduling (short/medium/long) and a stride-aware prefetcher that groups pages likely to be served by the same kernel to improve kernel batching efficiency
Backpressure policy: when decoder queue exceeds low/med/high thresholds, throttle prefill work first (deferred bucket) and prioritize short-decodes to preserve p50 latency

Trade-offs considered: affinity improves kernel utilization but risks staleness; we add a lightweight aging policy and on-miss feedback so affinity adapts. Compaction lanes increase code complexity but limit H-O-L interruptions from heavy compaction
Interaction with existing KV invariants: maintain existing checksum and tenant isolation semantics; compaction must be crash-safe and atomic per-page
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (design + prototype): implement page residency scoring and simple light-lane reclamation; add tracing hooks to measure page churn (2w)
Phase 2 (affinity + scheduler): add kernel-affinity map and bucketed prefill scheduler; implement stride-aware grouping heuristic and backpressure thresholds (3w)
Phase 3 (compaction lanes): introduce heavy-lane compaction with safety checks and instrumentation; add periodic maintenance job with rate-limits (2w)
Phase 4 (perf runs + tuning): run mixed-workload replay, iterate on thresholds and affinity aging, measure cost impact and regressions (2w)
Phase 5 (canary rollout): gated flag + deploy to dedicated canary pool, monitor p99/p50, token-cost, and errors for 72 hours before gradual rollout (1w)
Phase 6 (cleanup + docs): address review feedback, add config knobs to Console, write runbook entries and failure-mode docs (1w)
test_plan: Unit tests for residency scoring, affinity map serialization, and compaction state machine
Integration test: synthetic mixed short/long workload that asserts no memleak and bounded decoder backlog
Perf harness replay: use 10 production traces (anonymized) with mixed lengths. Measure p50/p95/p99 and token cost delta
Chaos test: kill runtime during heavy-lane compaction and assert page integrity after restart
E2E canary metrics: runtime traces, token billing simulation, and Console dashboard snapshots
rollout_plan: Feature flag default=off. Enable on internal dev clusters for smoke tests
Canary: enable on 5 dedicated nodes handling non-critical tenant traffic for 72h
If canary health OK (no SLO regressions and p99 improvement observed), enable on Dedicated slice with gradual ramp to 20% of traffic
Full rollout conditioned on 7-day stability and product sign-off
Rollback: flip flag off; compaction is designed to be reversible with no state loss
monitoring: New traces: page_gc.duration, page_gc.type (light|heavy), affinity.hit_rate, prefill.backlog_size
Dashboards: p50/p95/p99 prefill latency by tenant and kernel-variant, token-cost delta, compaction rate
SLO alerts: prefill.p99 > baseline * 1.25 triggers PagerDuty; affinity.hit_rate < 0.6 for 5m triggers Paging as warning
Health checks: memory occupancy heatmap and compaction queue depth
